Aki 0.3.1

Fix

  • Pointing inside apps that tell macOS nothing about their window (Telegram) now picks the message, button or icon under the pointer. In 0.3.0 it still took the whole window there.

Aki 0.3.0

Mark anything, even where apps say nothing

  • Apps that don't tell macOS what's in their window (Telegram, games, some design apps) and pages drawn as one picture (Google Sheets): Aki now finds the box under the pointer in the screen itself — a message, a row, a button, an icon, a photo, a single spreadsheet cell. ↑ takes what holds it.
  • ⇧-click is a normal click on the app below (another sheet, a tab, a menu), without making a mark. A point is now ⌘-click.
  • ⌘+ / ⌘− zoom the page below while you mark.
  • Zoom on any mark's picture, from the card, the queue or the History.

The queue

  • Shows every mark, can be moved out of the way, and marks can be ticked and removed together (⌫).
  • The History shows what's waiting in the queue: keep marking with it, drop one, or clear it.

Faster, and to the right session

  • Marking opens at once, with the session you last wrote in as the destination.
  • The session picker shows four sessions, the rest behind "+N", each with whether it's working or waiting for you.
  • Marks go to the terminal 3 s after you stop (was 5 s).
  • Updates are announced, not downloaded: a pill by the sidebar and a dot on the menu bar pin.

Fixes

  • Sessions take the name you gave their tab in Orca.
  • Marks reach Orca tabs again after Orca restarts.
  • The sidebar's resize corner works next to the last ring.

Aki 0.2.0 — the first version for everyone

Mark anything

  • Mark an element, an area or lines of text in any app with ⇧⌘A. Chrome, Brave, Edge, Arc and Vivaldi give the exact element (selector, text, HTML, React source), no extension needed.
  • Arrow keys walk the page like DevTools.
  • Each mark carries its text and, when it helps, a crop.
  • A queue: send one, send all, or keep them for later. Queued marks survive restarts.

Your agents

  • One ring per Claude Code or Codex session, showing the AI and the app it runs in.
  • Marks go to the right session by themselves, then Aki types the request into its tab, with a countdown and a ✓ when the agent is done.
  • MCP server and aki command for any agent, aki:// links and Raycast commands.

Around it

  • History (⇧⌘H) with search and filters.
  • Get started: every permission, why it's needed, and a button straight to it.
  • Nine languages, light and dark, shortcuts you choose, and updates by itself.
  • Secrets on screen are never read; the local server is locked to your Mac; updates are signed.
